correctness.rationale: For every S of size <=n-2 and every matching T within S, the remaining 2k>=4 vertices have original forbidden-pair edges of degree <=1 and at most k-2 further forbidden queried edges; residual degree >=k gives a perfect matching by Dirac. For matching |S|=n-1, every proper trace is realized using complement of two matchings (Dirac for 2k>=6, K4 three pairings for 2k=4); full trace requires a legal remaining pair. A support with intersecting edges has no full trace, and an n-edge matching fails a last-negative trace. The top support is in unique bijection with a complete pairing plus its omitted edge; lower coefficients follow inclusion-exclusion. All smaller faces extend to a facet, so the complex is pure. The positive-root induction bounds online shattering depth. The independent-enumeration program checks 104500 supports n=2..5 and every small-support trace; this corroborates but cannot replace the unlimited proof.

originality.rationale: A complete all-support Boolean shattering classification for nonbipartite deranged pairings is not stated or implied by the inspected primary results or closest retrieved records. Existing exact perfect-matching total counts are expressly credited, not claimed new. The strong bipartite crown analog has no degree-(n-1) shattered faces, whereas the present class has n*p_n; full priority remains unproved.
residual_risks: Possible unindexed sharp E(m,n) statement for cocktail-party graphs in older restricted matching extension literature.
Some class of perfect-matching trace configurations might have been described without VC terminology under preclusion or matching-covered-system language.
The known deranged-pairing count p_n is not a new fact; its combination with newly proved support identification is the result under assessment.
Full historical priority, external checking, and homotopy classification remain unestablished.

value.rationale: Natural full learning complexity of deranged complete pairings, not a routine total-count exercise: the result identifies all Boolean supports, including a sharp one-degree last-pair boundary, produces the full f polynomial and a pure complex, and establishes equality of VC and adaptive shattering dimensions. It explains a qualitative difference from bipartite derangements, whose similar-looking perfect-matching incidence system loses the top degree. Standard p_n enumeration is explicitly credited and only structural implications are assessed as new.
